title: Organ flue pipe
summary: This model speaks the wrong mode. At the measured foot pressure of 360 Pa the real pipe speaks its first mode, but the default jet sounds the second (1051 Hz), and the forced Bickley jet sounds a high mode between 4.7 and 7.4 kHz. Which high mode it sounds depends on the recorded window of the jet response, which does not converge on this pipe. The pipe is one open tin flue pipe measured by M. Castellengo (ISMA 2004): bore, mouth, flue, foot pressure, pressure threshold and first resonance (475 Hz). It is built from those measurements alone and blown at that pipe's own measured foot pressure. The jet is wrong, not the pipe data. At 360 Pa the jet leaves the flue at 24.45 m/s, so the Strouhal number fW/U over the 7 mm cut-up is 0.139 for the first mode and 0.278 for the second. The jet cards on this route select modes at two to three times the Strouhal number at which a real flue pipe speaks (open work: pexfp.135.6, parked; the resolved jet, pexfp.138). Not graded: the screened organ references are registrations at Eb3, A2 and Gb6, none within an octave of this pipe, so the renders are checked against the pipe's own measurements instead.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop on the generic flue network route (music_render wind): a jet driven by the measured foot pressure acting on a connected duct network, the same route and modules as the recorder, tin whistle and pan pipes, with no organ-shaped code

the measured pipe as data (data/instruments/geometry/organpipe-tin-principal-castellengo2004): a 27 mm bore running 308.5 mm from the mouth centre to the open end, and a mouth 21 mm wide with a 7 mm cut-up. The flue is 0.25 mm, the centre of the paper's 0.2 to 0.3

the mouth's acoustic mass from its 3-D geometry: the 21 by 7 mm cut through the wall of the 13.5 mm bore, closed flush at the languid, with free space outside, solved as potential flow on a staircase of cut cells (fs_bem::wall_window, three grids extrapolated at the order they show) in place of the 0.61 a_eq mouth inertance. It is 31.78 mm of bore with a 0.5 mm wall and 32.91 mm with 0.7 mm, the two ends of the unstated wall's bracket. The mouth radiates from the outer face of the same solve on the pipe's rigid outer cylinder

the measured wind: the pipe's steady foot pressure of 360 Pa, reached by the paper's short attack through its two stated points (125 Pa at 9 ms, 360 Pa at 45 ms); a second card per jet raises the pressure from 0 to 360 Pa over the paper's four-second slow rise

dry room air at 20 C (organ wind is room air; the laboratory's temperature and humidity are not stated); fractional-delay propagation and gas-derived viscothermal loss on the bore; compact baffled radiation at the open end

a passive resonator that lands near the measured one: the first resonance predicted from the network (bore, computed mouth mass, baffled-piston end, wall dispersion) is 486 Hz with the length read from the languid, or 476 Hz read from the upper lip; the paper measured 475 Hz. The paper does not say where its 312 mm is measured from, so neither reading is chosen. With the default jet at 22 and 67 Pa the pipe sounds its first mode at 490 Hz

two jet laws on the same pipe, both rendered: the default card's authored jet (the repository's interim slot-jet card, displacement gain 90, as on every other flue card) and the forced Bickley jet (jet_response forced-bickley 0.1 180, uniform exit: half-width 0.19 mm, Reynolds number 304, station 37 half-widths)
physics_missing: the register: the real pipe speaks its first mode at 360 Pa and has a static threshold of 125 Pa. The default jet sounds the second mode at 360 Pa (1051 Hz, fW/U 0.30), with the third and fifth harmonics stronger than the fundamental. On the slow rise it sounds from about 14 Pa and is mostly in the first mode up to 90 Pa (the second at 45 Pa). It then sounds the fourth and third modes between 135 and 225 Pa and the second from 247 Pa: falling through the modes as the pressure rises, where the pipe climbs. The forced jet sounds a high mode at 360 Pa, and the band below 2 kHz is 69 to 77 dB down. With the card's window of 180 it is near the tenth mode, 4.68 kHz, whose third harmonic is the strongest line. That frequency is not a result. Doubling the grid spacing to 0.2 moves the line by 0.8 cents, but windows of 90 and 360 put the dominant line at 6.37 and 7.44 kHz instead. Only this holds: at no window does the forced jet sound the first or second mode. On the slow rise it is in the second mode by 22 Pa and moves irregularly through higher modes to 4.2 to 4.5 kHz, never sounding the first. A probable reason: a jet that does not spread (the module does not claim spreading) grows high frequencies far more than the first mode's over its 37 half-width station. The module's gain per mode was not measured. In the real pipe, high-mode mouth tones appear only in the transient (paper Sec. 3)
a reference: the screened organ recordings are registrations at Eb3, A2 and Gb6, none within an octave of this pipe, and no open-access measured pipe at those pitches was found

a spectrum like a real pipe: odd harmonics only (the labium offset and jet angle are not stated and are zero), and both jets put most of their energy above 2 kHz, where the receiver is not valid (compact baffled radiation, ka <= 0.5 on the 13.5 mm end). Raising the bore's loss and phase bands from 3 to 11 kHz changes neither render (0.0 dB on the default jet; the forced jet's lines unchanged), so that energy is the jets' own and not a band edge of the loss

the wall thickness, the point the 312 mm length is measured from, the upper lip, the flattened mouth, the flue's depth and the languid, the foot and toe hole, and the room: not stated (unknowns.tsv). The foot's own acoustics are absent because the cards drive the flue with the measured foot pressure

mouth tones, chiff and wind noise of the attack: the paper's whole subject. The route has no hydrodynamic feedback from the labium to the flue and no resolved jet, so it cannot make edge tones (audit row N8)
native verification beyond one binary, one seed and the stated numerical checks
